deep.reconstruction:
This page finishes the 'Hilbertian tensor product' section of a 1953 expository draft on functional analysis. It then moves on to Hilbert–Schmidt operators.

(1) Theorem 1. Let E be a Hilbert space and μ a positive (Radon) measure on a locally compact space M. The previous page built the map L²(μ)⊗E → L²_E(μ), φ⊗a ↦ φ·a. It preserves the inner product, since (φ·a, ψ·b) = (φ,ψ)(a,b), and its image is dense. So it extends to an isometric isomorphism from the Hilbert completion L²(μ) ⊗̂₂ E onto L²_E(μ), the space of square-integrable E-valued functions.

(2) Corollary 1 is the case of counting measure on a discrete set I: l²(I) ⊗̂₂ E = l²_E(I). The right side is the space of square-summable families (x_i) in E, with inner product Σ(x_i, y_i).

(3) Corollary 2. For (M,μ) and (N,ν), L²(μ) ⊗̂₂ L²(ν) = L²(μ⊗ν), using the product measure on M×N. The proof goes through L²(μ⊗ν) = L²_{L²(ν)}(μ), which is a Fubini-type statement, and then applies Theorem 1 with E = L²(ν). Taking discrete spaces gives l²(I) ⊗̂₂ l²(J) = l²(I×J), which recovers an earlier Prop. 1.

(4) New topic. For Hilbert spaces E and F, identify the dual E' with the conjugate space Ē (Riesz). Then Ē⊗F corresponds to the continuous finite-rank operators E→F, via (ā⊗b)x = (x,a)b.

The next page shows that the operator norm is at most the Hilbert tensor norm, so the map extends injectively to Ē ⊗̂₂ F. Its image is defined to be the Hilbert–Schmidt operators. This is the standard Hilbert–Schmidt identification, set up as a preliminary to Grothendieck's general programme on topological tensor products.
errors: No real errors. Corollary 2 relies on the identification L²(μ⊗ν) ≅ L²_{L²(ν)}(μ), which is only asserted ('on a un isomorphisme canonique'). For arbitrary (non-σ-finite) Radon measures, and for measurability of the L²(ν)-valued sections, this needs the Bourbaki framework (density of compactly supported continuous functions, Lusin measurability). The page does not address these points, though the claim is true in that setting.

ideas.what: Hilbert completion of L²(μ)⊗E equals the Bochner/Bourbaki space L²_E(μ)
ideas.modern_name: Hilbert space tensor product; L²(μ;E) ≅ L²(μ) ⊗̂₂ E
ideas.where_published: Possibly in Grothendieck's São Paulo lecture notes 'Espaces vectoriels topologiques' / Produits tensoriels topologiques background (unsure)

ideas.what: l²(I) ⊗̂₂ E = l²_E(I) and L²(μ) ⊗̂₂ L²(ν) = L²(μ⊗ν)
ideas.modern_name: Tensor product of L² spaces equals L² of the product measure

ideas.what: Finite-rank operators E→F identified with Ē⊗F via (ā⊗b)x = (x,a)b, extended to Hilbert–Schmidt operators
ideas.where_published: Background in 'Produits tensoriels topologiques et espaces nucléaires' (Memoirs AMS 16, 1955) and the Résumé (1953)

deep.surprise_reason: Standard textbook material on Hilbert tensor products and Hilbert–Schmidt operators, written up expositorily. Nothing beyond the well-known theory.
transcription_corrections: 'Théorème 1 (10)': the '(10)' is likely a misreading. Equation (10) is already the inner product on the previous page, so this is probably just 'Théorème 1' with a stray mark or '(1°)'.
Corollary 2: 'Alors E [?] on a un isomorphisme' should read 'Alors on a un isomorphisme canonique'. The 'E' is probably a false start.
The last lines plausibly read: 'En particulier, si L²(μ) et L²(ν) sont l²(I) et l²(J), on retrouve la prop. 1.'
The '!' after formula (14) is an emphasis or reminder mark, not part of the formula.
